questions.q: What is a 'constitution' in the context of Constitutional AI?
options: A single hard-coded rule that overrides all model outputs
A written, curated list of principles the model should follow, used both to self-critique responses and to guide AI preference judging
The hyperparameter configuration file for PPO training
A legal document unrelated to model training
questions.explain: The constitution is an explicit, written set of principles — drawing in part on sources like the UN Declaration of Human Rights — adapted into instructions the model applies when critiquing, revising, or judging.

questions.q: What happens in Constitutional AI's phase 1 (the supervised phase)?
options: A reward model is trained directly on human preference data

The model generates an initial response, critiques it against a constitutional principle, revises it based on that critique, and the revised responses become new supervised fine-tuning data, producing SL-CAI
PPO fine-tunes the model directly against a reward model with no critique step
The model is evaluated against held-out preference accuracy
questions.explain: Phase 1 is a supervised critique-and-revision loop whose output (revised responses) becomes SFT data, producing the SL-CAI model.

questions.q: What happens in Constitutional AI's phase 2, and how does it map onto Chapter 7's RLHF structure?
options: It discards the SL-CAI model and starts RL from the original pretrained base model

An AI judge compares response pairs from the SL-CAI model against the constitution's principles, those labels train a reward model, and PPO fine-tunes SL-CAI against it — mirroring Chapter 7's reward-model-then-PPO structure, producing RL-CAI
It trains the reward model on human-labeled data exclusively, with no AI judge involved
It skips reward model training and applies DPO directly on the constitution text
questions.explain: Phase 2 is RLAIF specifically guided by the constitution: AI preference labels train a reward model, and PPO fine-tunes the SL-CAI model against it, exactly mirroring the RM-then-PPO structure from Chapter 7.

questions.q: Why does writing the constitution's principles down explicitly matter, compared to an unconstrained judge prompt like 'which response is better?'
options: It doesn't matter — both approaches produce identical, interchangeable results

An unconstrained prompt leaves criteria implicit and inconsistent across phrasing, while an explicit written constitution is inspectable, editable, and applies consistently across both the critique and judging steps
Explicit principles make the model unable to generate any critique at all
Written principles are only usable in phase 2, never in phase 1
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that an explicit constitution is auditable and editable without retraining from scratch, and keeps criteria consistent across both phases, unlike an implicit, prompt-dependent judge criterion.

questions.q: What are the names of the models produced by phase 1 and phase 2, respectively, in Anthropic's Constitutional AI paper?
options: SFT-model and PPO-model
SL-CAI (from phase 1's supervised critique-and-revision) and RL-CAI (from phase 2's RL fine-tuning)
RM-CAI and DPO-CAI
Base-CAI and Final-CAI
questions.explain: The paper names the supervised-phase output SL-CAI and the RL-phase output RL-CAI, matching the two-phase structure described in this lesson.
